nodes.name: One-pot solvothermal sulfur passivation
nodes.procedure: The one-pot solvothermal process was employed to construct the Co₃O₄-S cathode, and thioacetamide was utilized as the sulfur source (0.2 mmol) to passivate the Oᵤ atoms of Co₃O₄, resulting in S content of 0.22 wt.% which exhibits the highest hydrogenation activity.
nodes.source_text: The one-pot solvothermal process was employed to construct the Co₃O₄-S cathode, and thioacetamide was utilized as the sulfur source to passivate the Oᵤ atoms of Co₃O₄. When the amount of S source is 0.2 mmol, the S content is 0.22 wt.% in the Co₃O₄-S cathode, which exhibits the highest hydrogenation activity.

nodes.description: LSV curves for electrocatalytic hydrogenation of CN⁻, NO₃⁻, CO₂, O₂

performance.value: higher polarization currents, lower onset potentials

nodes.source_text: From the results of the linear scanning cyclic voltammetry (LSV) curves, the Co₃O₄-S cathode has higher polarization currents and lower onset potentials in the presence of CN⁻, NO₃⁻, CO₂, or O₂, indicating its extraordinary reduction activity and sluggish HER kinetics (Figure 3a).

nodes.description: CN⁻ reduction Faradaic efficiency at different potentials
nodes.source_text: With the increase of potentials from -0.1 to -1.1 V vs RHE, the faraday efficiency (FE) of CN⁻ hydrogenation into NH₃/CH₄ and CH₃NH₂ increases first and then decreases. The highest FE of CN⁻ hydrogenation on the Co₃O₄-S cathode (45.3%) is achieved at -0.6 V vs RHE, which is significantly higher than that of Co₃O₄ (19.6%)

nodes.description: NO₃⁻ reduction Faradaic efficiency at different potentials
nodes.source_text: The FE of NO₃⁻ hydrogenation into NH₃ over Co₃O₄-S cathode reaches 100% at -0.4 to -0.8 V vs RHE (Tables S4 and S5, Supporting Information), much higher than Co₃O₄ cathode (31.2% - 83.0%) (Figure 3f). The highest yield of NH₃ reaches 11.0 mmol h⁻¹ m⁻² over the Co₃O₄-S cathode, which is 2.8 times that of the Co₃O₄ cathode

nodes.description: Practical CN⁻ mineralization in flow system with real wastewater

wastewater.value: CN⁻: 152.9 mg L⁻¹, TN: 90.3 mg L⁻¹

nodes.source_text: a flow electrocatalytic system was constructed for practical metallurgical wastewater treatment (CN⁻: 152.9 mg L⁻¹; TN: 90.3 mg L⁻¹)... 100% of CN⁻ and 95% TN are continuously removed in the flow electrocatalytic system within 144 h, and no Co ions are leaching observed

The cyclic voltammetry (CV) was thus carried out... The intensity variation of the oxidation peak for adsorbed *H is ≈2.3 times that of Co₃O₄... stronger H* characteristic signals and higher H* concentrations are monitored in EPR technology over the Co₃O₄-S cathode (6.8×10⁻⁶ mol L⁻¹) than over the Co₃O₄ cathode (3.0×10⁻⁶ mol L⁻¹)

It can be found that the onset potential of HER shifts observably to a more negative value, and the reduction peak disappears with the increase of S contents into Co₃O₄ (Figure S15, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: No significant difference between Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄-S in the X-ray diffraction spectrum.
nodes.evidence_snippet: There is no significant difference between Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄-S in the X-ray diffraction spectrum (Figure S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₃O₄-S presents the same hexaentous star structure as Co₃O₄ with S uniformly distributed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: according to the results of scanning electron microscope and energy dispersive spectrometers mapping, Co₃O₄-S presents the same hexaentous star structure as Co₃O₄, and S is uniformly distributed on Co₃O₄ (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: S is uniformly distributed on Co₃O₄ in Co₃O₄-S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: according to the results of scanning electron microscope and energy dispersive spectrometers mapping, Co₃O₄-S presents the same hexaentous star structure as Co₃O₄, and S is uniformly distributed on Co₃O₄ (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: No new Co-S bond peaks appear after S modification; F₂g, E_g, and A₁g peaks in Co₃O₄-S are slightly red-shifted due to decreased Co-O bond energy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 2a, after modifying with S, no new characteristic peaks of the Co-S bond appear, indicating that S does not directly bind to Co atoms. The typical three peaks of F₂g, E_g, and A₁g in Co₃O₄-S are red-shifted slightly, which results from the introduction of S decreases the bond energy of Co-O.

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Co K-edge EXAFS peak intensity weakens and FT-EXAFS/WT-EXAFS peaks shift positively after S introduction, confirming S stretches Co-O bonds without direct Co-S binding.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peak intensity of normalized K-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) is weakened after the introduction of S into Co₃O₄ (Figure 2b). The characteristic peaks of Co₃O₄-S in Fourier-transformed extended XAFS (FT-EXAFS) and wavelet-transformed extended XAFS (WT-EXAFS) are more positive than Co₃O₄ (Figure 2c; Figure S3, Supporting Information). These results further confirm that S does not directly bind to Co atoms, and the introduction of S stretches the Co-O bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p XPS peaks consistent between Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄-S with no significant shift; S 2p XPS shows S-O bond at 170.5 eV (SO₄²⁻) with no Co-S bond; O_U peak area decreases after S introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All peaks in Co 2p X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) of Co₃O₄-S are consistent with those of Co₃O₄, and their position does not shift significantly... As can be seen from the S 2p XPS (Figure 2d), the peak at 170.5 eV is attributed to the S-O bond of SO₄²⁻, and no Co-S bond is detected... After the introduction of S, the peak area of O_U decreases observably.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR peak intensity decreases with increasing S source due to bonding of unpaired electrons in O_U.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peak intensity in the EPR spectroscopy decreases with the increase of the S source. This is because the unpaired electrons in O_U are bonded...

nodes.characterization_summary: Three types of oxygen atoms present: lattice oxygen (O_L), bridging oxygen (O_B), and unsaturated oxygen (O_U); O_U content decreases from 26.7% to 13.1% after S introduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The CO₂-temperature-programmed desorption (CO₂-TPD) curves exhibit that there are three kinds of oxygen atoms in Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄-S... The content of O_U significantly decreases from 26.7% to 13.1% after the introduction of S.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows stronger C≡N (530 cm⁻¹), C-N (980 cm⁻¹), N-H (1640 cm⁻¹), and C-H (2330 cm⁻¹) signals on Co₃O₄-S than Co₃O₄; E_g (480 cm⁻¹) and A₁g (690 cm⁻¹) modes vibrate confirming H* migration to Co sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A similar conclusion can be obtained from the results of the in situ Raman spectra (Figure 4g). The peaks at 530, 980, 1640, and 2330 cm⁻¹ are the Raman signals of C≡N, C-N, N-H, and C-H bonds. The stronger intensity of these peaks is observed in the Co₃O₄-S cathode than in the Co₃O₄ cathode.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ DRIFTS shows peaks at 1070 cm⁻¹ (-NH₂), 1360 cm⁻¹ (-CH₃), 1630 cm⁻¹ (C=N) with increased intensity and decreased -OH peak (~3300 cm⁻¹) on Co₃O₄-S vs Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: three peaks located at 1070, 1360, and 1630 cm⁻¹ present in the in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS), which are attributed to the vibration of -NH₂, -CH₃, and C=N bonds, respectively. After the passivation of O_U atoms with S, the intensity of these peaks significantly increases, and the intensity of the -OH peak (around 3300 cm⁻¹) decreases...
